column1: # Who each siglum is, from Campaner's own introduction (leaves 15-22), which
# this edition otherwise drops. The general abbreviation list on leaf 25 gives
# only `G. T.—Guillermo Terrassa.`; the eight leaves before it give the man, his
# trade, what the manuscript physically is, the years it covers and where it was
# in 1881. Without that a siglum is initials, and the chronicle's whole point is
# that you can ask which manuscript reports what.
# Entered by hand from the transcription of those leaves, and every row carries
# the leaf it comes from so that any claim here can be checked against the
# facsimile. Nothing is inferred: where Campaner does not say, the field is
# empty. `life` and `role` are his statements, not ours -- he took most of them
# from Bover's `Biblioteca de Escritores Baleares` and says so.
# Prose is Catalan because it is shown on the site; manuscript titles keep the
# spelling Campaner prints, in Spanish or in Mallorcan as he found them.
